title: X Corp and SpaceXAI drop antitrust lawsuit against Apple
excerpt: The companies moved to dismiss claims that Apple illegally shut out rivals by integrating ChatGPT into its devices, but will continue pursuing OpenAI
content_html:
X Corp and SpaceXAI moved to resolve their claims against Apple on Monday, filing to dismiss an antitrust lawsuit that accused the iPhone maker of conspiring with OpenAI to monopolize markets for smartphones and generative AI chatbots, according to Reuters.

No explanation for the dismissal appeared in the court filing, and it gave no indication of whether the parties had agreed to a settlement, according to CNBC. Elon Musk's companies, Apple, and OpenAI did not respond to requests for comment.

The lawsuit, filed in federal court in Texas last year, alleged that Apple broke antitrust law when it embedded ChatGPT from OpenAI into the Apple Intelligence suite across iPhones and other Apple devices. X and SpaceXAI contended that Apple, working in concert with OpenAI, had foreclosed competition, with the suit alleging the two companies "locked up markets to maintain their monopolies and prevent innovators like X and xAI from competing."

X and SpaceXAI indicated that their legal fight with OpenAI is ongoing, as the company remains named in the suit. Apple contended, in pushing for dismissal, that nothing in its arrangement with OpenAI prevents the latter from working with competitors, while OpenAI characterized Musk's legal offensive as "a campaign of lawfare" against it. Both companies denied any wrongdoing.

A judge ruled in November that the case could move forward, a preliminary victory for Musk's companies. A separate Musk lawsuit against OpenAI, which accused the company of straying from its founding mission to build AI for humanity's benefit rather than profit, was thrown out in May.

SpaceXAI is a division of SpaceX.
